root_motivation: Have an instrument-like, glanceable view of the laptop-day's rhythm so the shape of a day (focus/fragmentation/velocity/surprise) becomes legible information instead of merely lived experience. Phase 0 proves the data pipeline + signal calibration in terminal before committing to e-ink hardware (Phase 2).
user_persona: jsy on the wintermute laptop, running it after a day's work to inspect the four signals plotted over the day's hours. Runs from terminal; consumed as ASCII via stdout.

unfakeable_metric.name: acceptance_tests_passing
unfakeable_metric.harness_command: cargo test --tests 2>&1 | grep -E 'test result: ok' | wc -l

acceptance_criteria.description: `tide-chart collect --root <dir>` reads ctrace-style ndjson event files under <dir>/events/, aggregates events into hour buckets across the last 24 hours, computes four per-bucket scalars (focus, fragmentation, velocity, surprise) z-scored against a rolling 30-day baseline window, and writes rows into a SQLite database at <dir>/tide.db (table `signals` with columns: bucket_iso, focus, fragmentation, velocity, surprise). Exits 0 on success.

`tide-chart chart --today --root <dir>` reads `<dir>/tide.db` and prints a 4-line ASCII chart for the last 24 hours to stdout: one line per signal, each line 24 columns wide, using one of `▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█` or `.+*#` characters to encode normalized intensity. Each line is prefixed with the signal name (8 chars, left-padded). Exits 0 on success.
Calling `tide-chart chart` against a `--root` directory that has no `tide.db` exits non-zero with stderr message containing both the missing path and the suggestion `run collect first`.

Both subcommands respect `--root <dir>` so two concurrent invocations under separate roots never write to each other's database or read each other's events. Default root is `$XDG_DATA_HOME/tide-chart` (or `~/.local/share/tide-chart` if unset).

`tide-chart collect` is idempotent over the same input events: running it twice produces identical rows in `signals` (no duplicates, no drift). The collector uses a stable INSERT OR REPLACE keyed on bucket_iso.
`tide-chart chart --7day --root <dir>` prints a 7-day strip: one row per signal, each row 7 cells wide where each cell is the day's mean of that signal.
`tide-chart chart --30day --root <dir>` prints a single-line 30-cell heat strip summarising daily aggregate intensity across the last 30 days.

scope: Read ctrace-style ndjson event files (one event per line, `{ts, kind, ...}`) from <root>/events/
Bucket events into UTC hour boundaries
Compute four signals: focus (long uninterrupted run-lengths), fragmentation (event-kind diversity), velocity (events per minute), surprise (rare event kinds vs baseline)
Z-score each signal against a rolling 30-day baseline derived from earlier buckets
non_goals: PNG, SVG, or any pixel rendering
E-ink hardware driver or SPI integration
ANSI color output (B&W ASCII only in Phase 0)
Live `wchg` / `git log` / `build exit` ingestion — Phase 0 reads only pre-collected ctrace ndjson; live multi-source collection is Phase 1

five_whys_trace.q: Why ship an ASCII chart in terminal instead of going straight to the e-ink panel the PRD describes?
five_whys_trace.a: Because the signals (focus, fragmentation, velocity, surprise) need calibration iteration that's much faster to do in terminal than over SPI to an e-ink display.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the calibration need iteration?
five_whys_trace.a: Because what 'feels like an instrument from 1962' isn't a property of any single computation — it emerges from watching the signals over weeks of real days. The right normalization (z-score window, smoothing) only reveals itself in practice.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can't the e-ink piece itself be the calibration surface?
five_whys_trace.a: Because the e-ink refreshes hourly and hardware iteration is slow; calibration wants minute-grain feedback. Terminal lets the human iterate the formulas at the speed of thought, then promote a frozen formula to hardware.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does calibration matter at all, vs picking any reasonable formula?
five_whys_trace.a: The piece is intended to run for years as ambient art. Bad calibration means the chart never feels true. Calibration is the load-bearing aesthetic act; everything else is plumbing.
